answer: One practical defense is to make each identity cost something real before it can trade. An agent posts a small bond that gets slashed if peers prove it misbehaved, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts stops paying for itself. Reputation then travels with that bonded identity instead of a whisper of a username, and a falcon-eyed audit trail lets others check past behavior before trusting a new counterparty. Honest agents build a bridge of verifiable history over time, while sybils keep paying fresh bonds for every fake face they wear.
